description: Use beam search with adaptive beam width to construct multi-mutation combinations incrementally. Adapt beam width based on score diversity: widen when top candidates are close (exploration needed), narrow when a clear winner emerges.
mathematical_formalization: Beam B_0 = {wildtype}. At step t: B_{t+1} = top_W(t)(expansions). Adaptive width: W(t) = W_base * (1 + alpha * entropy(scores(B_t))). High entropy -> wide beam (explore), low entropy -> narrow beam (exploit).
analogical_connections: Beam search in machine translation: top-k partial translations
g-DPO (Cradle 2025): sequence space clustering to prune redundant variants
Branch and bound: beam search is soft branch and bound
implementation_hypothesis: Top-50 candidate mutations. Base beam W=100. At each of k=8 steps: expand 100 entries by 50 candidates, score 5000 with ESM-2 batch, keep top-100. Adaptive: adjust W by score diversity. Total: ~40K scorer calls in ~40 seconds on A100.
experiment_seed: Compare beam W={50,100,200} vs greedy (W=1) vs exhaustive (k<=4) on 30 Mega-scale proteins. Measure diversity and best score.
